Git.check: The project is a git repository, and every finished task is its own commit.

Branches.check: Build work happens on a branch, not directly on the main branch.

venv.check: Packages install into an environment that belongs to this project only, and a fresh install from the requirements file works.

Env vars.check: Settings that differ per machine come from the environment, and the app starts from the example env file once its values are filled in.

Secrets.check: The real env file is ignored by git, and no key or password appears in the code, the git history or the logs.

CLAUDE.md.check: CLAUDE.md exists, names the check command and links to the plan.

Modularity.check: Each file has one job that can be said in one line, and no file has become a catch-all.

Separation.what: Separation of concerns: keep screens, rules and data apart
Separation.check: Screen code, business rules and data access live in separate places, and the rules can be tested without the screen.

Webhooks.applies: another service must tell the app when something happens, such as a payment
Webhooks.check: A webhook with a missing or wrong signature is refused, and the same webhook delivered twice has the effect of one.

HTTP status codes.check: Errors return the matching status code (not found, not allowed, bad input), never a success code with an error inside.

Edge front door.applies: the app is going live on the internet

Databases.check: Data that must last is stored in a database and is still there after the app restarts.

Data modeling.check: Each kind of thing has its own table, tables are linked, and no fact is stored in two places.

Migrations.applies: the app uses a database with tables
Migrations.check: Every change to the tables is a migration file in the project, and a fresh database built from the migrations works with the app.

Transactions.applies: one action changes several records that must stay in step
Transactions.check: When a save with several steps fails partway, none of its steps stay saved. A test forces the failure.

Threat modeling.applies: the app has logins, money or private data

Least privilege.applies: the app uses keys, database users or service accounts
Least privilege.check: Each key and database user can do only what the app needs. No admin or root key is used while the app runs.

Secure defaults.check: With a setting missing, the app takes the safe path: debug mode off, new things private, access refused.

Secret rotation.applies: the app is live and uses long-lived keys

Authentication.check: Pages and actions for logged-in users refuse a visitor who is not logged in, including direct requests that skip the screen.

OAuth 2.1.applies: users log in with Google or another provider
OAuth 2.1.check: Login through the provider works end to end, and the app never sees or stores the provider password.

Magic links.applies: users log in with an email link
Magic links.check: A login link works once and expires after a short time. A used or expired link shows a clear message.

Multi-factor auth.applies: accounts guard money or sensitive data

API keys.applies: the app gives keys to its users or to other programs
API keys.check: A new key is shown once and only its hash is stored. A revoked key stops working at once.

Unified principal.applies: callers arrive in more than one way, such as a login and an API key

Hashing.what: Store a one-way fingerprint of a password, never the password
Hashing.check: Passwords are stored only as salted hashes made by a password-hashing function. No password appears in the database, logs or error messages.

Brute force.applies: users log in with a password
Brute force.check: Repeated wrong passwords for one account, or from one source, are slowed down or locked out.

Authorization.check: Every action checks on the server that this user may do it. Hiding a button does not count as the check.

Owner-only access.applies: users have their own private data
Owner-only access.check: A logged-in user who asks for another user's item by its id is refused, for reading, changing and deleting.

Role-based access.applies: the app has more than one kind of user, such as admin and member
Role-based access.check: Each role can do exactly its allowed actions. A test tries each forbidden action as each role.

Input validation.applies: the app accepts input from users or other systems
Input validation.check: Every input is checked on the server for type, size and allowed values. Bad input gets a clear error and is never saved.

XSS.applies: a web app shows text that users typed
XSS.what: Cross-site scripting: stop user-typed text from running as code in someone else's browser
XSS.check: Text containing a script tag, saved by one user, shows as plain text to another user and does not run.

CSRF.applies: a web app keeps users logged in with cookies
CSRF.what: Cross-site request forgery: stop another site from acting through a logged-in user's browser
CSRF.check: A request that changes something, sent from another site without the app's token, is refused.

CORS.applies: a browser frontend calls an API at a different address
CORS.what: Cross-origin resource sharing: decide which other sites may call your API from a browser
CORS.check: The API allows only the app's own frontend addresses, and never every site together with logins.

SSRF.applies: the server fetches addresses that users supply
SSRF.what: Server-side request forgery: stop users from making your server fetch internal addresses
SSRF.check: A user-supplied address that points at this machine, a private network or a cloud metadata address is refused.

SQL injection.applies: the app uses a SQL database
SQL injection.check: Every query passes user input as parameters. Input containing quotes and SQL words is treated as plain text.

Content Security Policy.applies: a web app is going live

Safe user HTML.applies: users can post formatted text or HTML
Safe user HTML.check: User HTML is cleaned to an allowlist of tags before it is shown. Scripts and event handlers are stripped.

Path & upload safety.applies: users upload files, or a file path comes from user input
Path & upload safety.check: Uploads are limited by type and size and stored under a generated name outside the code folder. A file name containing ../ cannot escape the upload folder.

Open redirect.applies: the app redirects to an address taken from a link, such as after login
Open redirect.check: A redirect target outside the app's own addresses is ignored.

TLS.applies: the app is going live on the internet

Encryption at rest.applies: the app stores highly sensitive data

Secure cookies.applies: a web app keeps users logged in with cookies
Secure cookies.check: The login cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.

PII minimization.check: Every personal field the app collects is used by a feature in the plan. Nothing is collected just in case.

Security headers.applies: a web app is going live

Trusted client IP.applies: the app sits behind a proxy and uses the visitor's address

Signed device ID.applies: the app must recognise visitors who have no account

Honeypot.applies: the app is live and being probed

Audit trail.applies: staff change other people's data, or money moves

Dependency scanning.check: A scan of the project's packages reports no known serious problems.

Secret scanning.check: A secret scan over the code and the full git history finds nothing.

Data retention.applies: the app keeps personal data over time

Consent management.applies: the app tracks visitors where consent is required

Design for failure.applies: the app depends on outside services

Bulkheads.applies: one failing part could take down the rest

Error budgets.applies: a team must balance new features against stability

Chaos testing.applies: the app runs on several machines

Timeouts.check: Every outside call has a time limit. With a service that hangs, the app gives up and tells the user.

Retry.check: A call that fails briefly is retried a few times with growing waits, then gives up with a clear error. Errors that can never succeed are not retried.

Circuit breaker.applies: an outside service fails often under real use

Error handling.check: A failure shows the user a plain message and is logged with detail. No raw error or stack trace reaches the screen.

Idempotency.applies: an action must never happen twice, such as a payment, an order or an email
Idempotency.check: The same request sent twice, by a double click or a retry, has the effect of one.

Fallback.applies: a feature should keep working when one part fails

Graceful degradation.applies: a feature should keep working when one part fails

Free-first cascade.applies: the app pays per call for data it could often get free

Concurrency gate.applies: heavy requests arrive faster than the app can serve them

Single-flight.applies: many identical requests arrive at once

Per-host pacing.applies: the app calls rate-limited outside services heavily

Quota ledger.applies: several workers share one limited key

Degrade under quota.applies: the app can run out of a paid quota

Rate limiting.applies: the app is going live with public or costly endpoints

Background jobs.applies: some work takes longer than a few seconds, such as sending email or calling an AI model
Background jobs.check: Slow work runs outside the request. The user gets an immediate response and can see the job's status.

Dead-letter queue.applies: background jobs fail under real use

Idempotent ingest.applies: the app receives messages from other systems
Idempotent ingest.check: The same incoming message delivered twice is processed once.

Health probes.applies: the app is live and depends on outside services

Race conditions.applies: two requests can change the same thing at once, such as stock, seats or a balance
Race conditions.check: Two requests at the same moment for the last item: exactly one succeeds. A test fires them together.

Optimistic locking.applies: two people can edit the same record

Backups & restore drills.applies: the app is going live with data worth keeping

Profiling.applies: something is slow and the cause is unknown

Latency percentiles.applies: speed must be measured under real traffic

Core Web Vitals.applies: public web pages are going live

Slow-query monitoring.applies: the database is under real use

Caching.applies: the same costly work is repeated often

Cache invalidation.applies: the app caches data that changes

Negative caching.applies: lookups that find nothing are repeated often

Dynamic TTL.applies: cached items go stale at different speeds

HTTP caching & ETags.applies: clients fetch the same responses repeatedly

Semantic caching.applies: many users ask an AI model similar questions

Indexing.applies: tables have grown and lookups are slow

N+1 queries.applies: lists show related data from the database
N+1 queries.check: Loading a list runs a small, fixed number of queries, not one per item. A test counts them.

Connection pooling.applies: the app is live and opens many database connections

Materialized views.applies: an expensive report is read often

Bulk operations.applies: the app writes many rows at once

Pagination.check: Long lists load a page at a time. No request returns every row.

Async I/O.applies: one worker must handle many waits at once

Bounded fan-out.applies: the app runs many outside calls in parallel

Debounce & throttle.applies: the screen fires rapid triggers, such as search while typing
Debounce & throttle.check: Typing quickly in a live search sends one request after the pause, not one per key.

Pre-aggregation.applies: counts and totals are slow to compute live

Load balancing.applies: one server is no longer enough

Autoscaling.applies: traffic rises and falls a lot

Sharding.applies: one database can no longer hold the data

CDN & edge.applies: users are far from the server

Code splitting.applies: the first page load has become heavy

Image optimization.applies: a web app with images is going live

Compression.applies: a web app is going live

Structured logs.check: The app logs errors and key events with a time, a level and a message, and never logs a secret or a password.

Metrics.applies: the app is live and its health must be watched

Request IDs.applies: a problem must be followed across logs

The four golden signals.applies: the app is live and its health must be watched

Per-job metrics.applies: background jobs run under real use

Upstream probes.applies: the app is live and depends on outside services

Actionable alerts.applies: the app is live and sends alerts

On-call and paging.applies: a team keeps the app running

Runbooks.applies: the app is live and things have gone wrong before

Upstream call log.applies: the app calls paid outside services

Cost alerts.applies: the app is going live and uses pay-per-use services

Feature flags.applies: features must be switched without a new release

Staged rollout.applies: a bad release would hit many users

Kill switch.applies: a live feature may need to be stopped fast

Streaming.applies: users wait on screen for an AI answer
Streaming.check: The AI answer appears on screen as it is generated, and a failure partway shows a clear message.

Prompt caching.applies: the app sends the same long prompt often

Structured output.applies: the app's code uses an AI model's answer
Structured output.check: AI output used by code is checked against a schema. A malformed answer is retried or refused, never passed on.

Model selection.applies: the app calls an AI model
Model selection.check: The model name is pinned in one setting, not scattered through the code or left to a moving default.

Non-determinism.applies: the app calls an AI model
Non-determinism.check: Tests of AI features assert facts that must hold, never the exact wording.

Prompt injection.applies: an AI model reads content its user did not write, or can take actions
Prompt injection.check: Text planted in content the AI reads, telling it to ignore its rules, does not change what the app does or reveal private data.

Jailbreak resistance.applies: the public can chat with the app's AI

Content moderation.applies: the public can post content or see AI output

PII redaction.applies: personal data is sent to an AI model
PII redaction.check: Personal details the model does not need are removed before the text is sent.

Output guardrails.applies: AI output triggers actions or is shown as fact
Output guardrails.check: AI output is checked before it is acted on, and an answer outside the allowed bounds is blocked.

Evals.applies: an AI feature is central to the app
Evals.check: Each prompt has a small set of example inputs with facts the answer must contain, run as a test.

LLM-as-judge.applies: AI output quality must be graded at volume

A/B testing.applies: there is enough traffic to compare two versions

LLM tracing.applies: AI features run under real use

Budget caps.applies: the app calls a paid AI model
Budget caps.check: A usage limit per user, and one overall, stops AI calls when reached and shows a clear message.

Batch API.applies: large AI jobs can wait for their results

Unified interface.applies: the app uses more than one AI provider

RAG.applies: an AI model answers from the app's own documents
RAG.check: Answers come from the retrieved documents. A question with no matching document gets an honest 'I don't know', not an invented answer.

Citations.applies: an AI model answers from the app's own documents
Citations.check: Each answer shows which documents it used, and each reference opens the right source.

Conversation memory.applies: the app has an AI chat
Conversation memory.check: A follow-up question that depends on earlier messages is answered correctly, and a long chat stays within the model's limit.

Knowledge freshness.applies: the documents an AI model answers from keep changing

Autonomy guardrails.applies: an AI model in the app can take actions that change things
Autonomy guardrails.check: Actions that change or delete things need the user's approval, and each run has a cap on its number of steps.

Live prompts.applies: prompts need tuning while the app is live

Prompt versioning.applies: prompts change while the app is live

Safe templates.applies: users can edit templates the app fills in

Payments.check: Card details go straight to the payment provider, and the app never receives or stores a card number. A test-mode payment completes end to end.

Webhook fulfilment.check: Access is granted when the provider's signed webhook arrives, not when the browser returns. A fake webhook is refused, and a repeated one grants once.

Subscriptions.check: Subscribing, renewing, cancelling and expiry each change the user's access correctly, driven by the provider's events in test mode.

Failed payments.check: A failed renewal marks the account as past due, tells the user, and removes access after the grace period.

Money as cents.applies: the app stores or calculates money
Money as cents.check: Amounts are stored and calculated as whole cents. Adding 0.10 and 0.20 gives exactly 0.30.

File uploads.check: A valid file uploads and can be opened again. A file that is too large or of the wrong type is refused with a clear message.

Full-text search.check: Search finds items by words in their text, handles no results, and returns only what this user may see.

Realtime updates.applies: changes must appear without a refresh
Realtime updates.check: A change made in one window appears in another within seconds without a refresh, and the connection recovers after it drops.

Scheduled jobs.applies: some work runs on a clock
Scheduled jobs.check: The job runs on schedule, a repeated or overlapping run does no double work, and a failure is logged.

Admin panel.applies: someone must manage the app's data
Admin panel.check: Only admins can open the admin area. A normal user is refused on every admin page and action.

Accessibility.check: Every page works by keyboard alone, form fields have labels, and an automated accessibility scan reports no serious problems.

Responsive design.applies: the app is used on different screen sizes
Responsive design.check: Every screen is usable at phone width: nothing cut off, no sideways scrolling, buttons large enough to tap.

Screen states.applies: the app has screens that load data
Screen states.check: Every screen that loads data shows a loading state, an empty state and an error state. Tests force each one.

Localization.applies: the app must work in more than one language
Localization.check: All visible text comes from translation files. Switching language changes every screen, including right-to-left layout where the language needs it.

Store times in UTC.applies: the app stores dates or times
Store times in UTC.check: Times are stored in UTC and shown in the user's time zone. A test with two time zones agrees.

Component library.check: Buttons, inputs and dialogs come from one shared set of components, not restyled page by page.

Guessable IDs.applies: ids appear in links or in the API
Guessable IDs.check: Ids in links and API responses are not counting numbers. Changing an id by one finds nothing.

Account recovery.applies: users log in with a password
Account recovery.check: A reset link works once and expires. The reset page gives the same answer whether or not the email has an account.

Soft delete.applies: users can delete things that matter to them
Soft delete.check: A deleted item disappears for the user and can be restored for a set period.

Testing.check: Every feature has tests for the normal case and at least one failure case, and the check command runs them all.

Playwright.check: The main user journeys run as automated tests that click through the real app.

CI/CD.what: Run the checks automatically on every change, and release automatically when they pass

Domain & DNS.applies: the app is going live on the internet

noindex.applies: a web app with private pages is going live

Social preview.applies: public web pages are going live
